description: The House Democratic Policy and Communications Committee (DPCC) is seeking a motivated, digital-savvy fellow to join an aggressive communications team for the Fall 2026 fellowship term (approx. mid-September through mid-January). This digital fellowship includes the production of high-quality web graphics and videos, as well as assisting with events and various projects to further House Democrats' work and messaging. This is a 4-month fellowship with a $3,200 a month stipend. The fellowship is full-time and in-person in Washington, DC. Deadline to apply: 5PM on Wednesday, September 2, 2026.
responsibilities: Production of high-quality web graphics and videos
Assisting with events and various projects to further House Democrats' work and messaging
Working on multiple projects at once under tight deadlines
qualifications: Strong technical skills
Advanced creativity and artistic ability
High level of attention to detail
Knowledge of Adobe Creative Suite (Premiere, Photoshop, InDesign)
Knowledge of Microsoft Excel/Google Sheets
Good team player
Willing to work on multiple projects at once
Able to work under tight deadlines
how_to_apply: Submit all application materials via the online form.

description: The Office of Congressman Salud Carbajal (CA-24) is seeking a highly motivated and creative Digital/Press Intern to assist with a fast-paced communications operation based in his Washington, D.C. office for the Fall 2026 term (August/September - December). The Digital/Press Intern will help build out the Congressman's digital and social media footprint, with heavy emphasis on creating engaging social media content and graphics. The intern will work closely with the Communications Director, Digital/Creative Assistant, Legislative Aide/Correspondent, and Scheduler. The internship will run from late August / early September to December 17. The hours are roughly 32 hours a week and are flexible to accommodate schedules but generally run 9 AM to 6 PM ET when Congress is in session and 9 AM to 5 PM ET when Congress is out of session. This position is in-person. This is a full-time, limited term position and offers a $1,500 monthly stipend from the office of Congressman Carbajal unless the intern is already receiving credit/stipend through a third party. Deadline to apply is Wednesday, August 26, 2026. However, candidates are encouraged to apply early, as applications will be reviewed and the position filled on a rolling basis.
responsibilities: Compiling daily press clips
Creating engaging graphics and editing photos
Assisting the Digital/Creative Assistant with social media content, website content and digital newsletters
Clipping, editing, and captioning videos
Assisting with press releases, op-eds, advisories, and other written materials
Creating and maintaining press lists
Compiling regular comms reports on press and social media results

Assisting the Legislative Aide/Correspondent and Scheduler with administrative tasks (e.g. answering phone calls, greeting visitors, etc.) and legislative tasks (e.g. batching incoming messages on Fireside, drafting constituent letters, writing cosponsor recommendations, etc.)
qualifications: Strong writing, editing, and social media skills
Basic familiarity with graphic design/video editing software
Experience in a press or digital media role (including internships) preferred but not required
Strong social media and graphic design skills
Experience with Canva, Photoshop, and other digital/graphic/video design platforms is a major plus
California or Central Coast ties are a plus
Spanish literacy is a plus
how_to_apply: Email a resume, cover letter, writing sample, two digital samples, and dates/hours of availability to Tommy.Vo@mail.house.gov with the subject line "First Name Last Name – Digital Intern." No phone calls or walk-ins.
equal_opportunity: This office is an equal opportunity employer and encourages candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply.

description: Law clerks will have the opportunity to work with the Committee's policy, oversight, and investigative teams, conducting legal and policy research, reviewing documents, and preparing materials for hearings, markups, and other Committee activities. The fall clerkship period runs from September to December. This is a paid position, and the Committee is happy to work with applicants seeking academic credit. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.
responsibilities: Conducting legal and policy research
Reviewing documents
Preparing materials for hearings, markups, and other Committee activities
qualifications: Current law student
Strong research and writing skills
Enthusiastic about the Committee's mission to protect the homeland and strengthen national security
Preference given to candidates available at least three days per week
how_to_apply: Submit a resume, brief cover letter, and writing sample to CHSJobs@mail.house.gov with the subject line "Fall Law Clerkship." Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

description: Representative Seth Magaziner (RI-02) seeks part-time, paid Fall 2026 interns for his Warwick, Rhode Island office, to start at the beginning of September and go until end of December. Duties include providing a welcoming environment to constituents, answering incoming calls, assisting Member and key staff with logistical and administrative duties, receiving and logging constituent input on policy matters, conducting research, drafting correspondence and memoranda, assisting with planning and execution of Member's public outreach at local events, and accompanying district staff to public forums, meetings, and events.
responsibilities: Provides a welcoming environment and positive first impression of the Member office to constituents, visitors, and other VIPs
Answers incoming calls with poise, professionalism, and promptness
Assists Member and key staff (e.g. Staff Assistant, Press Assistant, Constituent Services Team) with logistical and administrative duties
Receives and logs input from constituents on policy matters for the Member office's consideration and response
Conducts research, and drafts correspondence and memoranda
Assists with planning and execution of Member's public outreach at local events
Accompanies district staff to public forums, meetings, and events as a representative to the Member
qualifications: Strong interpersonal and communication skills
Professional phone manner
Ability to conduct research and draft correspondence
Organizational skills for administrative and logistical support
Interest in constituent services and public outreach

description: The House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform Democratic Staff seeks a motivated and reliable Video Production Intern this fall. Interns will be responsible for helping with clipping streams of sessions, editing and captioning videos, helping with shoots, scripting content and other administrative tasks as assigned. Successful candidates will possess extreme familiarity with Adobe Premiere Pro. Additional experiences with Adobe After Effects and Photoshop are a plus. Ability to work in a fast-paced, rapid response environment is a must. Candidates will be expected to work in-person in Washington, DC, with opportunities for remote work during Congressional recesses. Full-time candidates with diverse backgrounds and experiences are strongly encouraged to apply. To apply, please send a resume, portfolio, and your availability this fall to ethan.cesar@mail.house.gov and OversightPress@mail.house.gov.
responsibilities: Clipping streams of sessions
Editing and captioning videos
Helping with shoots
Scripting content
Other administrative tasks as assigned
qualifications: Extreme familiarity with Adobe Premiere Pro
Ability to work in a fast-paced, rapid response environment
Additional experience with Adobe After Effects and Photoshop is a plus
how_to_apply: Send a resume, portfolio, and your availability this fall to ethan.cesar@mail.house.gov and OversightPress@mail.house.gov.

description: Congresswoman Doris Matsui, representing the 7th Congressional District of California, seeks interns for her Washington, D.C. office for the Fall 2026 term. The Press and Digital Intern will help communicate the Congresswoman's work through social media, graphics, photography, video, and other digital content. This position is well suited for a creative candidate who is interested in public service and eager to build communications experience in a congressional office. Washington DC interns may be asked to assist in researching legislation for the Member and legislative staff, attending briefings, hearings, and markups, and responding to constituent correspondence. Ties to California's 7th District are preferred, but not required. All applications are considered on a rolling basis.
responsibilities: Communicate the Congresswoman's work through social media, graphics, photography, video, and other digital content
Answer phones and perform data entry
Assist in researching legislation for the Member and legislative staff
Attend briefings, hearings, and markups
Respond to constituent correspondence
qualifications: Strong writing, editing, and social media skills
Basic familiarity with graphic design/video editing software
Experience in a press or digital media role (including internships) preferred but not required
Familiarity with Canva, photography, video editing, or graphic design
Interest in digital marketing, audience engagement, or social media analytics
Strong media literacy, attention to detail, and sound judgment
Ability to listen closely, follow instructions, learn through observation, and willingness to try new approaches
Ties to California's 7th District preferred but not required
how_to_apply: Visit the "Internships" page of Congresswoman Matsui's official website and complete the application form: https://matsui.house.gov/services/internships. Submit a cover letter, resume, and 2 writing samples (1 writing sample & 1 graphic example preferred, but not required).
equal_opportunity: This office is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate based on race, religion, disability, age, ethnicity, national origin, sex, gender, LGBTQ identification, family status, or military status.

description: Congresswoman Doris Matsui, representing the 7th Congressional District of California, seeks interns for her Washington, D.C. and District (Sacramento) offices for the Fall 2026 term. Interns will have a unique opportunity to learn about the legislative process firsthand and the many functions of a Congressional office. Intern responsibilities will vary but may include answering phones and data entry. Washington DC interns may be asked to assist in researching legislation for the Member and legislative staff, attending briefings, hearings, and markups; and answering constituent letters on various issues. Interns based in California may also be asked to assist on a variety of constituent casework or in-district projects, as needed. To apply, please visit the "Internships" page of Congresswomen Matsui's official website and complete the application form: https://matsui.house.gov/services/internships. As part of the application, a cover letter, resume, and 2 writing samples are required. Ties to California's 7th District are preferred, but not required. All applications are considered on a rolling basis. This office is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate based on race, religion, disability, age, ethnicity, national origin, sex, gender, LGBTQ identification, family status, or military status.
responsibilities: Answering phones
Data entry
Researching legislation for the Member and legislative staff (DC interns)
Attending briefings, hearings, and markups (DC interns)
Answering constituent letters on various issues (DC interns)
Assisting with constituent casework (District interns)
Assisting with in-district projects as needed (District interns)
qualifications: Ties to California's 7th District are preferred, but not required
Cover letter required
Resume required
2 writing samples required
how_to_apply: Visit the "Internships" page of Congresswoman Matsui's official website and complete the application form at https://matsui.house.gov/services/internships. A cover letter, resume, and 2 writing samples are required. Applications are considered on a rolling basis.
equal_opportunity: This office is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate based on race, religion, disability, age, ethnicity, national origin, sex, gender, LGBTQ identification, family status, or military status.
